hero.title: State Executive: Governor
hero.description: Master the constitutional office of the Governor (Articles 153 to 162, 163, 164, 200, 201, 213)—including appointment methods, executive/legislative powers, discretionary privileges, pardoning limitations, veto paths, and comparisons with the President of India (UPSC GS Paper-II: Indian Polity).

mockIntro.title: Interactive UPSC Mock Test
mockIntro.description: Evaluate your understanding of Articles 153-162, Governor's dual role, discretionary powers, pardoning powers under Article 161, and bills reservation under Article 200.

timeline.title: Key Milestones & Judicial Landmark Decisions
timeline.description: Important constitutional milestones and landmark Supreme Court verdicts concerning the discretionary powers and office of the Governor.

cards.details: Amended Article 153 to facilitate the appointment of the same person as Governor for two or more states.

cards.period: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
cards.details: Supreme Court held that the Governor's assessment regarding the breakdown of constitutional machinery is subject to judicial review, and the floor of the Assembly is the only forum to test a majority.

cards.period: Rameshwar Prasad v. Union of India
cards.details: The Supreme Court ruled that the Governor cannot recommend dissolution of the Assembly under Article 356 based on subjective claims of horse-trading unless a floor test is conducted.

The Supreme Court clarified that the Governor's discretionary power under Article 163 is limited, and the Governor cannot act independently of the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers in summoning or dissolving the Assembly without valid constitutional grounds.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Hacks
mnemonics.description: Quick memory triggers to retain Governor-related Articles and constitutional features.

items.title: Mnemonic 1
items.decryption: Governor's details: President appoints (Art 155), Agreeable term of office (Art 156), Qualifications (Art 157), Conditions of office (Art 158), Oath or affirmation (Art 159), Discharge of functions in contingencies (Art 160).

items.title: Mnemonic 2
items.decryption: Recall that while 123 is for the President, switching the first two digits to 213 yields the Ordinance-making power of the Governor.

items.title: Mnemonic 3
items.decryption: Remember Article 200 is the gateway through which the Governor assents, withholds, returns, or reserves state bills for the President.

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Active-recall review of the Governor's constitutional powers and limitations.

items.question: Can a Governor pardon a death sentence under Article 161?
items.answer: No. The Governor has no power to pardon a death sentence. The Governor can only suspend, remit, or commute a death sentence. The President holds the exclusive power to pardon death sentences under Article 72.

items.question: Is the Governor's office considered an employment under the Central Government?
items.answer: No. The Supreme Court in 1979 ruled that the office of Governor is an independent constitutional office and is not an employment under the Central Government, nor is it subordinate to it.

items.question: What happens if a Governor reserves a bill for the President's consideration?
items.answer: Under Article 201, the President can either give assent, withhold assent, or direct the Governor to return the bill to the State Legislature. If returned, the legislature must reconsider it within 6 months. Even if passed again, the President is not bound to give assent.

items.question: What is the minimum age qualification required to be appointed as a Governor?
items.answer: A candidate must have completed the age of 35 years and must be a citizen of India.

items.question: Can the Governor nominate members to the State Legislative Assembly?
items.answer: No. Previously, the Governor nominated 1 member of the Anglo-Indian community if underrepresented. However, this nomination was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019.

traps.title: UPSC Civil Services Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Assuming that the Governor has the same security of tenure as a Judge or the President. No! The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156). The Constitution does not lay down any grounds or procedure (like impeachment) for the removal of the Governor.

Trap 2: Believing the Governor's advice mechanism is identical to the President's. Unlike Article 74 which leaves the President with no explicit discretionary powers, Article 163 explicitly grants the Governor discretionary powers. If any question arises whether a matter falls under the Governor's discretion, the decision of the Governor is final.

Trap 3: Assuming the Governor can promulgate ordinances at any time. The Governor can only promulgate ordinances under Article 213 when the State Legislature (or both houses in a bicameral state) is not in session. Additionally, the Governor cannot promulgate certain ordinances without prior instructions from the President.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Comprehensive structured analysis of the Office of the Governor.

sections.title: 1. Constitutional Position & Dual Role
sections.content:
Dual Role of the Governor

The Governor functions in a dual capacity: (1) As the constitutional head of the state, bound by the aid and advice of the state Council of Ministers (Article 163) for most tasks, and (2) As a representative of the Union Government, acting as a crucial link between the Centre and the States. This dual role often becomes a source of tension in center-state relations.

Constitutional Convenants:

  • Article 153: A Governor for each State (or 2+ states under 7th Amendment).
  • Article 154: Executive power of the State is vested in the Governor.
  • Article 156: Holds office during the pleasure of the President, up to a normal term of 5 years. Can resign by writing to the President.
  • Article 163: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor, except in matters where the Governor is constitutionally required to act in his discretion.

sections.title: 2. Executive, Legislative & Veto Powers (Art 200 & 201)
sections.content:
Veto Options under Article 200

When a bill passed by the state legislature is presented to the Governor, the Governor has 4 choices: (1) Give assent, (2) Withhold assent, (3) Return the bill (if not a Money Bill) for reconsideration, or (4) Reserve the bill for the consideration of the President. Reserving is compulsory if the bill endangers the position of the State High Court.

Power CategoryKey Constitutional Actions & Limitations
Executive PowersAppoints Chief Minister, Council of Ministers, Advocate General of the State, and State Election Commissioner. Recommends state emergency (Art 356).
Legislative PowersSummons/prorogues the State Legislature, dissolves State Assembly. Nominates 1/6th members of State Legislative Council in bicameral states.
Financial PowersLays State Budget (Annual Financial Statement) before legislature. Money bills can only be introduced with his prior recommendation.

sections.title: 3. Pardoning (Art 161) vs President & Ordinance-Making (Art 213)
sections.content:
Pardoning Power (Article 161 vs Article 72)

The Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment for offenses against a state law. However: (1) The President can pardon sentences by a Court Martial, while the Governor cannot. (2) The President can pardon a death sentence, whereas the Governor CANNOT pardon a death sentence (the Governor can only suspend, remit, or commute it).

Ordinance-Making Power (Article 213)

Promulgated during recess of the State Legislature. It has the same force as an Act of the State Legislature but must be approved within 6 weeks of reassembly (maximum life is 6 months + 6 weeks). Presidential Instruction requirement: The Governor cannot promulgate ordinances without instructions from the President if a bill containing the same provisions would have required Presidential assent.
